knowledge.label: START WITH YOUR KNOWLEDGE
title: “Where was that file?”
Let’s move beyond that.
knowledge.body: The documents exist, but finding them takes time. Questions pile up with the person who knows. Akarel helps make organizational knowledge useful in everyday work.
rows: Internal documents, policies, manuals and past materials. RAG—retrieval-augmented generation—provides a foundation for using your own information, beyond generic answers.
Built around the language of work.
Which information matters? What questions come up? We understand the work and help organize the knowledge and how people use it.

agents.label: AI AGENTS
title: Beyond search.
Towards the next action.
agents.body: Combine organizational knowledge with workflows and decision rules. Research, summarize, draft and check. AI agents with roles tailored to specific tasks support everyday work.

agents.humanBody: We design the scope of delegation, review points and approval rules around the work.

security.label: SECURITY THAT FITS
title: Designed around
your organization’s standards.
security.body: Every organization handles information differently. We review your security standards and internal policies, then design and adapt Akarel’s environment, permissions and operations.

rows: Decide what AI can use and what must be excluded, based on confidentiality and operational needs.
Review which people and departments may access which knowledge.
Consider where information is processed and which services are used, in line with your environment and constraints.
Agree who reviews AI output and how knowledge is updated, with rules people can use in practice.

approach.label: BUILT AROUND YOUR WORK
title: Installing AI
is just the beginning.
approach.body: Understand the work first. Start small and improve how people use it. Together with BonZuttner’s hands-on support, we shape Akarel around daily operations.
rows: Review the challenges, information and security requirements.
Try it on a small scale
Focus on a specific task and validate responses and use with the people doing the work.
Update knowledge and rules so the service remains useful.

hero.title:
Build for the work.
Make it last.
hero.body: Business systems, web services and mobile apps. We understand the people and the work, then build together from requirements through design, development and operations.

starting.title:

“What if we could…?”
starting.body: You do not need a finished specification. Tell us about the daily work, the problems and what you want to make possible. We clarify what to build together.
points: Turn unclear needs into shared understanding.
Clarify the purpose, users and priorities in the language of the work. Use screens and prototypes to check that we are aligned.
Build something new or use what is already there.
Look at existing systems and operations, then choose an approach to improvement, integration or new development.

items: Design and build for the purpose

Validate behavior, permissions and security, and retain specifications, decision rationale and operating guidance for maintenance and improvement.

steps: Understand the work and users, then agree on scope and priorities.

Review working software and test quality and operations.
Support introduction and handover, and agree on maintenance and improvement.

title: Work alongside.
Get our hands dirty.
hero.lead: Building a system is not the goal. We learn the reality of management and frontline work, then stay close until the business and the work itself become stronger and easier to move forward.

reality.title:
Do not start with AI.
Do not start with a system.
Start with what is happening now.
body: You cannot see operational waste from a meeting room alone.

Those who lead.
Those who manage.
Those who do the work.
We listen to each, watch the work itself, and decide what should change.

Use AI when it helps.
Build a system when it helps.
Connect IoT when it helps.
But we do not build when it is not needed.

items.title: Remove before you build.
items.body:
Does this input need to exist? Why is this approval here? Why is the same information entered repeatedly?

We first organize the work itself. Remove what can disappear, change what can change, then implement AI or systems only where needed.

items.title: See numbers and strain.
items.sub: Operational KPIs alone do not change the frontline.
items.body:
We look beyond time, profit and cost to daily friction: searching, waiting, asking, transcribing and redoing.

Less overtime. Fewer questions. Less concentration on veteran staff. Better business numbers.
items.emphasis:
Do not reduce people.
Reduce friction in work.

items.title: Look beyond the screen.
items.sub: The frontline is not only inside a browser.
items.body:
Factories. Vehicles. Warehouses. Fields. Paper. Excel. LINE.

That is why we do not think in web or generative AI alone. We combine AI, business systems, IoT and location intelligence for the reality of the work.

technology.title:
Choose the means
for the problem.
technology.body: Sometimes changing a workflow or rule is enough. When technology is needed, we introduce it in a form the frontline can actually use.
items: Entering the same information again and again.
Review whether each input and approval is needed, then reduce remaining re-entry with existing tools and automation.
Asking someone whenever you need a document.
Organize where information lives and how it is shared, then use AI document search where it helps.
Management cannot see what is happening on site.
Review recording and reporting, using sensors or location data when needed to share information for decisions.

fde.title:
Sometimes it is called
an FDE approach.
body:
Forward Deployed Engineer.

It means entering a customer’s operation, understanding the challenge, implementing and staying involved until it is actually used. It is close to work we have long done.

But BonZuttner does not value an engineer visiting a site for its own sake.

Those who lead. Those who use. Those who build.
We help all three see the same problem. That is our accompaniment.

cases.title:
See the reality.
Then choose the technology.

items.title:
Untangle complex work
with the frontline.
items.body: We map production, review, approvals and store deliveries, then improve fragmented information, duplicate entry and manual checks. Workflow improvements and the system evolve together.

items.title:
Make everyday operations
stronger and smoother.
items.body: A BtoB wholesale platform connects administrator and store screens. Products, client-specific pricing, publication and order information are managed on the web, with continuous improvements for real operations.

items.title:
Free daily data entry
from manual work.
items.body: Back-office work relied on manual input and checks because external websites did not provide an API. We automated transfers from Excel to the web and browser operations, combining AI input assistance with data integration to reduce repetitive input and checking.

process.title:
Four moments
we move through together.
process.lead: Not just in a meeting room. We work until daily work changes, choosing the means only after seeing the reality.
steps: Hear the business aim and the voice of the frontline.
See the flow of work, information and friction together.
Organize the challenge and decide what changes first.
Combine AI, existing tools and operations until it sticks.

graduation.title:
So that one day,
it runs without us.
body: We do not think accompaniment means creating a state where improvement is impossible without us.

We leave what we build together as assets the customer can operate.

Everyday improvement stays inside. For the difficult parts, we work together again.

cta.title:
Tell us about
the work on the ground.
cta.body:
“It is vaguely inconvenient, but we have always done it this way.”

That kind of work contains the seed of improvement. Whether to use AI comes later.

title: A view from space.

satellite.0.lead: Farmland conditions, climate changes, logistics and assets. We combine satellite data with AI and field information to turn hard-to-see risks and changes into inputs for business decisions.

applications.label: TWO WAYS TO SEE
title: From places to observe,
to decisions that matter.
applications.note: These are example applications. The scope of analysis is designed around the region, observation conditions and available data.
rows: Which crops suit this land? How are the fields doing? Combining satellite imagery with climate and soil information supports crop planning and risk assessment for agricultural and resource businesses.
Compare land conditions with crop characteristics to explore what to grow and where.
Analyze crop and soil conditions from satellite imagery to understand farmland.
Use yield estimates and climate-related variability as inputs to procurement and business planning.
Observe changes across large areas, including places that are difficult to visit. Satellite data can inform logistics, asset and environmental decisions for trading companies and global businesses.
Study vessel movements and port congestion to consider bottlenecks and alternative routes.
Observe forest loss and land changes over time to understand environmental conditions.
Monitor conditions at overseas plants and mines to inform asset management and investment decisions.

implementation.label: SATELLITE × AI × IMPLEMENTATION
title: From analysis
to a useful system.
implementation.body: Define the question, analyze satellite data with AI and make the results easy to understand. Where needed, connect that insight to systems used in daily work.
rows: Select satellite imagery, climate, soil and other information for the purpose, then design the AI analysis.
Use a proof of concept to assess results and field use, then decide on the next stage.
From visualization and interface design to production systems and operation, implement in stages based on what the validation shows.

approach.label: FROM DATA TO DECISIONS
title: Not just data
on a screen.
approach.body: What do you need to know? Which decision will it inform? We define the analysis around that purpose. We do not treat satellite data as definitive on its own; on-site information and expert knowledge also matter.
rows: Agree on the location, period and use, then define what the analysis needs to answer.
Combine the data needed for comparison, analysis and visualization.
Share how to interpret results and their limits, so people can consider the next action.

site.0.label: DX & AI / System development / Our services
site.0.title:
Understand the work.
Change it with technology.
site.0.desc: We start with the “why” behind your operations, combining AI with expert judgment to build systems people actually use. BonZuttner works alongside you from process discovery through development and operations.
site.0.note: Challenges that are still hard to put into words are welcome.
site.0.attitude: Sincerity, with a spoonful of humor.
site.0.alt: An illustration of a diverse team having a natural conversation with a city and trees in the background
site.0.section: Real-world challenges don't fit neatly into service categories.
site.0.intro: We start by understanding both business priorities and day-to-day operations, then tailor our approach accordingly. By combining hands-on business support with technology development, we help businesses move forward.

groups.name: CLIENT SOLUTIONS
groups.label: Making change happen, together
groups.summary: We bridge the gap between frontline teams and management to improve daily operations, building sustainable systems where technology adds real value.
items: Drive meaningful improvements in business performance and operations.
From planning and development to launch and ongoing support.

groups.name: PRODUCTS & DATA
groups.label: Build and grow
groups.summary: We turn firsthand operational knowledge into innovative products and data services, combining product expertise, technology, and operations within one team.
items: AI agents powered by organizational knowledge and designed for specific tasks.
Location intelligence to help protect your valuable vehicles.
Smarter agricultural decisions powered by satellite data and AI.

difference.title: We do not stop at a polished proposal.
difference.desc: Rather than delivering solutions developed behind a desk, we work alongside your team to find practical answers together.
points: We observe how work really gets done, listen to the people involved, and uncover challenges that documents alone cannot reveal.
We don't develop new systems by default. If existing tools or improved processes can solve the problem, we start there.
Our commitment doesn't end with a proposal or launch. We continue supporting your team until the changes become part of everyday operations.

story.title:
Build the future
through what we do.
story.body: We believe everyone deserves a fair opportunity to turn their knowledge and aspirations into meaningful work, and that everyday dialogue and collaboration can help create a more peaceful world. BonZuttner was founded in 2019 to bring this vision to life through business.

members.title: The people who make things happen.
members.body: We listen, plan, work alongside our clients, and turn ideas into practical solutions. Our team brings together diverse expertise and backgrounds to achieve shared goals.

field.title:
Work we have
set in motion.
cases: We untangle complex frontline work and support the launch of the systems that follow.
Location intelligence and weather-risk alerts help protect valued vehicles.
We turn satellite data into practical insight for land analysis and decisions.

contact.title: Start with a challenge, even if it's not fully defined.
contact.body: It's okay if you're not sure where to start. We work with both frontline teams and management to identify challenges and find the best way forward together.

hero.label: OUR STORY / WHY WE EXIST
title: Through work,
toward peace.
hero.body: We connect people’s skills, experience, and aspirations with meaningful work and opportunities to contribute to society. Through dialogue, understanding, and creating value together, we believe we can move closer to peace.

beginning.label: OUR BEGINNING
title: Bridging talent
and opportunity.
body: Our journey began when we met skilled Syrian IT professionals who faced barriers to employment and fair compensation because of displacement or where they lived.

At the same time, businesses in Japan and beyond needed specialized technology expertise. We saw an opportunity to connect skilled professionals with those needs while delivering value to customers. BonZuttner was founded in 2019 as a systems development company.
beginning.source: Read the story behind our founding

name.label: THE NAME BONZUTTNER
title: Keep striving
to do good.
name.body: Our name honors Bertha von Suttner, a peace activist and Nobel Peace Prize laureate. Her commitment to peace inspires how we act every day. Our name also draws on three linguistic elements.
name.meaning: Someone who continually strives to do good—and follows through with action.

technology.label: WHY TECHNOLOGY
title: Working together
across borders.
body: Technology enables people in different places to bring their expertise together and deliver meaningful results. We chose this field to connect the skills of the people we met with work that addresses real needs in society.

AI can accelerate work and software development. But understanding business needs, designing reliable systems, and taking responsibility for quality, security, and ongoing operations still require professional expertise. We believe these skills will remain essential.
technology.note: Who does this technology serve, and how can we use it responsibly?

re.label: OUR THREE “RE” PRINCIPLES
title: A new beginning
for each person.
re.body: No one should be defined solely by displacement or nationality. Every person has a name, skills, character, and aspirations. Through meaningful work, we aim to create more opportunities for people to shape their own futures.
re.tabLabel: The meaning of our three Re. words
items: Build a new life in a new environment and reconnect with others.
Bring skills and experience to creating new value and a shared future.
With those renewed connections and possibilities, find a starting point to move forward.

future.label: THE FUTURE
title: Peace, through
everyday work.
body: Talk. Understand another person’s circumstances and efforts. Find grounds for empathy across differences, and build relationships. We want our business to help those relationships grow.
Keep a promise to a customer. Talk things through as a team. Help people find pride and choices through work. We hope these small, repeated acts contribute to peace in society.
future.closing: To hold hands, look forward, and gaze into the light.

next.label: MEET BONZUTTNER
title: Putting our beliefs
into action.
next.body: What could we achieve together, and who would you work alongside? Explore our services and meet the people behind BonZuttner.
